answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond and files one ivory carving in a public registry. Auditors verify it: an opal assay recomputes the refractive index, and a saffron weigh checks the packet weight. Reuse or a copied assay burns the bond. The k-th filing costs 38+7(k-1): 1,000 fakes pay 3,534,500 plus 70,000 locked against a 40,000 pool. A rented-carving ring fails: one carving cannot pass two assays. Honest agents file once, pay 38, reclaim it.
